newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt to resume Sao Paulo debt talks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt to resume Sao Paulo debt talks - paper.

text.p: The Brazilian state of Sao Paulo will resume negotiations with the federal government over its $54.2 billion debt on October 7 after talks were broken off in July, the O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper reported Saturday.

"We are working on some hypotheses which I cannot elaborate on but which will be explained to the governor when I return from the IMF meeting," Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola told the newspaper before leaving for Washington.
Loyola said that the Banco do Estado de Sao Paulo (Banespa) would be included in the discussions.
Banespa, owned by the Sao Paulo state government, was estimated to be holding $16.8 billion of the total Sao Paulo state debt owed to the federal government last March.

In the newspaper interview, Loyola stated: "The privatisation of (Rio de Janeiro state bank) Banerj has been put forward, we negotiated a deal with Minas Gerais which included the privatisation of Credireal and Bemge and now it is Banespa's turn."
Loyola would not say however if Banespa would be privatised.

Sao Paulo governor Mario Covas does not want the issue of Banespa's possible privatisation to be included in the talks and is seeking 30 years to repay the debt, the term already given to the states of Rio Grande do Sul and Minas Gerais, O Estado said.
Sao Paulo state, Brazil's most populous, constitutes the country's industrial heartland.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
